reviews.comment: Lectures were very confusing at times and he sometimes won't explain how he got an answer or how to approach the problem a different way. Tests were hard at first and were incoherent at times, but got better as the semester went on (last test and final were very fair/easier). Curved the class at the end.

You probably won't learn much, but at least he lowered the cutoff for an A. Grades very tough on exams (hardly gives back any partial credit). I think it's his first time teaching a class, so that's probably why he's not that good at teaching. I like how everyone suddenly likes this dude as soon as their grades are good.

The lack of any solid review material was very frustrating, as each exam (including the final) felt like I was going in completely blind. Quizzes were a lottery. Lectures got hard to follow later in the semester. Homework is at least forgiving. Seemed like he wanted to improve, so hopefully future semesters will be better.

I have accommodations and Prof. Sarvesh was very accommodating. He would give extensions whenever I asked him and would have office hours to accommodate my schedule. His additional office hours before exam was helpful!
Not bad. I got an A. I like his teaching style.

Exam: little partial credit, no review, no curves, hard exams, bad grading
Quizzes: 1 question, all or nothing
Lecture: behind syllabus & lab, bad handwriting, skips steps, incomplete examples b/c the rest is simple, many mistakes
No homework/quiz/lecture solutions for review. Quiz schedule, # of quizzes, and Zybook homework don't follow syllabus.

His lectures cover the material well and give good examples, but he moves on quickly and has messy handwriting which wouldn't be too bad if he just uploaded the lecture notes.

Tests are hard mostly due to time constraints and the minimal partial credit. Questions themselves are usually accessible not excessively hard.

Good guy. Alright teacher.

I registered for Dr. Miller and got this guy. Horrible during lectures, if you ask a question he we always raise his tone and say "I just went over this" and then not explain any further. Exams are difficult and the grading makes no sense. Do not take this guy

Messes up consistently where it seems like he is reading a script during lectures. Provides minimal help for homework or any questions in general(beats around the bush a lot). Provides no partial credit for some exam questions, you could've messed a sign on the final step and he might given you no credit or take half off. apathetic.

Refuses to give additional examples/resources to prepare students for exams even after being asked. Gives little to no partial credit on exams and doesn't grade fairly on questions with multiple parts. Doesn't "belabor the point" enough on difficult concepts, making lectures hard to follow. Do not take him if you care about your learning experience
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were very difficult to follow even though the examples were necessary to understand for the exam. Quizzes are often one or two questions every week and you get them or you don't. Little to no partial credit on exams. Often teaches material needed for the lab after we have had that lab.

So rude. It is impossible to ask for help in understanding anything without him having an attitude and being overwhelmingly rude. He also makes so many mistakes in lecture but will take off an insane number of points on exam for making a single mistake. He does not follow the mistake if the question is multipart. Zybooks grade is unclear as well.

Pros:
Doesn't give much work, usually once a week and has multiple attempts; good for learning.
Cons:
Doesn't give hardly any partial credit at all. Expect for chained free response answers to all be counted off if one part is wrong.
Unsympathetic to his students and their efforts. Bad with tech, his iPad always acts up. Was very behind in lecture.
Just a very average teacher. Grades pretty tough on exams. Also, he's a phD student, and not a professor yet.
